      <article class="
        prose prose-neutral dark:prose-invert prose-base lg:prose-lg

        <span id="hs_cos_wrapper_post_body" class="hs_cos_wrapper hs_cos_wrapper_meta_field hs_cos_wrapper_type_rich_text" style="" data-hs-cos-general-type="meta_field" data-hs-cos-type="rich_text"><p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Improving developer workflows means reducing inefficiencies and delivering software quickly without compromising quality.</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>If your team is struggling with slow development cycles, frequent context switching, lengthy </span><a href="/glossary/code-review" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>code reviews</span></u></a><span>, or excessive manual work, you need to optimize your operations. In this guide, we'll explore </span><strong><span>seven practical tips for improving developer workflows</span></strong><span>, which will help</span><strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"> </span></strong><a href="/blog/how-to-improve-developer-productivity" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>boost productivity</span></u></a><span>, streamline collaboration, and deliver high-quality software more efficiently.</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span></span></p><div class="hs-cta-embed hs-cta-simple-placeholder hs-cta-embed-171760058926" style="max-width:100%; max-height:100%; width:700px;height:137.953125px; margin: 0 auto; display: block; margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px" data-hubspot-wrapper-cta-id="171760058926" align="center"> 
 <a href="/hs/cta/wi/redirect?encryptedPayload=AVxigLLbdAL9l%2Bw4vxNcNTq8AeUKUXPSf8%2F1Q6lKlTnRlqJaMgimRJh7nWTu%2FQfrGMfr%2FDMN02xq5ZcxW17bpidPMyyUZddBiVfTaf7UeLe3oMIkB3TWzJ%2BHnKE4RjTqUVYED%2FGHz0Jd6%2FnmZlY3N3ID5FYYFgg4SN9ct93vOUhatebCeFe6dWFCzVr8rJctMJGOOnyoIud0Ng%3D%3D&amp;webInteractiveContentId=171760058926&amp;portalId=46014728" target="_blank" rel="noopener" crossorigin="anonymous"> <img alt="Follow AI Trends with Zencoder" loading="lazy" src="https://no-cache.hubspot.com/cta/default/46014728/interactive-171760058926.png" style="height: 100%; width: 100%; object-fit: fill; margin: 0 auto; display: block; margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px" onerror="this.style.display='none'" align="center"> </a> 
</div></span><p></p>
<h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Key Takeaways</span></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Use AI to eliminate repetitive development work</span></strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span><a href="/blog/best-ai-coding-assistants" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>AI coding assistants</span></u></a><span> can automate tasks such as writing boilerplate code, generating tests, </span><a href="https://zencoder.ai/blog/code-refactoring-techniques"><u><span>refactoring</span></u></a><span>, and </span><a href="/blog/best-code-documentation-tools" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>creating documentation</span></u></a><span>. Always review </span><a href="/blog/ai-code-generation-the-critical-role-of-human-validation" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>AI-generated code</span></u></a><span> to ensure it meets your quality and security standards.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Build a consistent workflow that your whole team follows</span></strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span><span>Standardized coding practices, Git workflows, pull request processes, and release procedures reduce errors, improve collaboration, and make projects easier to maintain as teams grow.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Keep changes small and automate testing whenever possible</span></strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span><span>Small, focused </span><a href="/glossary/pull-request" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>pull requests</span></u></a><span> are easier to review and merge, while automated testing catches bugs earlier and gives teams more confidence to release software quickly and reliably.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Measure impact, not just output</span></strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span><span>Lines of code and commit counts no longer reflect productivity in the age of AI. Focus on delivering valuable features, solving complex problems, reducing code churn, and improving overall software quality.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Simplify development with an all-in-one AI platform</span></strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span><span>Managing multiple AI tools can create unnecessary complexity. </span><a href="/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>Zencoder</span></u></a><span> combines coding assistance, testing, </span><a href="/blog/agentic-ai-vs-ai-agents" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>AI agents</span></u></a><span>, and </span><a href="/blog/ai-workflow-automation-for-developers-10-proven-patterns-to-ship-faster" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>workflow automation</span></u></a><span> in a single platform, helping teams streamline development, from planning to deployment.</span></li>
</ul>
<h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>7 Tips for Improving Developer Workflows in 2026</span></h2>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Here are </span><strong><span>seven practical tips </span></strong><span>to help you streamline development, improve collaboration, and ship high-quality software faster.</span></p>
<h3>1. Leverage AI-Assisted Development Tools</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>According to JetBrains, </span><a href="https://blog.jetbrains.com/research/2025/10/state-of-developer-ecosystem-2025/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>62% of developers</span></u></a><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"> </span><strong><span>rely on at least one AI coding assistant or editor</span></strong><span>. The reason is clear: These tools automate many repetitive tasks that slow developers down, including writing boilerplate code, generating tests, </span><a href="/blog/context-aware-code-completion-ai" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>suggesting code completions</span></u></a><span>, and </span><a href="/blog/code-refactoring-tools" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>refactoring code</span></u></a><span>.</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Here’s how to get the most out of AI coding tools:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Pick the right tool</span></strong><span> – Choose an AI coding assistant that fits your IDE, </span><a href="https://zencoder.ai/blog/ai-coding-languages"><u><span>programming languages</span></u></a><span>, development workflow, and security requirements. Also consider factors such as context awareness, integrations, pricing, and support for the tasks you perform most often.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Integrate AI into your workflow</span></strong><span> – Set up your AI assistant inside your IDE or editor so it becomes a natural part of coding, debugging, testing, and refactoring.</span></li>
<li><a href="/blog/ai-prompt-engineering-best-practices" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>Write effective prompts</span></u></strong></a><span> – Learn how to provide clear context, review AI-generated code carefully, and treat suggestions as a starting point rather than the final solution.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Use AI for repetitive work</span></strong><span> – Let AI handle boilerplate code, documentation, </span><a href="/glossary/unit-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>unit tests</span></u></a><span>, and routine refactoring so you can spend more time solving complex problems.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Review the output</span></strong><span> – Always verify AI-generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability before committing it to your codebase.</span></li>
</ul>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Here are some of the </span><a href="/blog/ai-tools-for-developers" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>best AI tools for developers</span></u></a><span> to consider:</span></p>
<div align="left">

<h3>2. Follow a Consistent Development Process</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Inconsistent workflows can slow development and make collaboration more difficult. When developers use different approaches for branching, testing, documenting, or deploying code, it's </span><strong><span>easier for mistakes to slip through</span></strong><span> and harder for teammates to work together efficiently. Here’s how to keep your workflow consistent:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Follow your team's coding standards </span></strong><span>– Write code that matches your project's style guide and conventions to keep the codebase consistent.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Use the established Git workflow</span></strong><span> – Adhere to your team's branching strategy and commit practices to ensure seamless code reviews and team alignment.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Write clear pull requests</span></strong><span> – Use your team's PR template, provide enough context for reviewers, and keep changes focused.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Stick to the release process </span></strong><span>– Follow the project's testing, deployment, and release procedures to reduce errors.</span></li>
</ul>
<h3>3. Keep Pull Requests Small and Focused</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Large pull requests take longer to review, are more difficult to understand, and often introduce bugs. Breaking work into smaller pull requests makes it</span><strong><span> easier for reviewers to provide meaningful feedback</span></strong><span> and reduces the risk of complex merge issues. Here’s how to improve your pull requests:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Focus on one change at a time</span></strong><span> – Keep each pull request limited to a single feature, bug fix, or refactoring task.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Avoid unrelated changes</span></strong><span> – Don't combine formatting updates, dependency upgrades, and feature work in the same pull request.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Merge regularly </span></strong><span>– Submit and merge smaller changes instead of waiting until a large feature is completely finished.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Break down large features</span></strong><span> – Divide complex work into smaller, independent pull requests whenever possible.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Write clear descriptions</span></strong><span> – Explain what changed, why it was needed, and what reviewers should pay special attention to.</span></li>
</ul>
<h3>4. Use Low-Code and AI for Rapid Prototyping</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Low-code platforms have become an increasingly popular way to accelerate software development, especially for internal tools, prototypes, and business applications. When combined with AI, low-code platforms help developers quickly validate ideas, automate repetitive tasks, and</span><strong><span> reduce the time required to deliver functional applications</span></strong><span>. Here’s how to use low-code effectively:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Choose the right projects</span></strong><span> – Use low-code for internal tools, dashboards, prototypes, and simple business applications rather than performance-critical or highly complex systems.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Combine low-code with AI</span></strong><span> – Use AI to generate forms, workflows, data models, and other repetitive components to speed up development.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Know when to write code</span></strong><span> – Switch to traditional development when you need greater flexibility, performance, or custom functionality.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Follow team standards</span></strong><span> – Ensure low-code applications meet your organization's security, documentation, testing, and deployment requirements.</span></li>
</ul>
<h3>5. Prioritize Automated Testing</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><a href="/blog/ai-vs-manual-unit-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>Manual testing</span></u></strong></a><strong><span> is difficult to sustain </span></strong><span>as applications become larger and more complex. By automating your tests, you can identify issues earlier, reduce debugging time, and release new features with greater confidence. Consider automating the following:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Unit tests </span></strong><span>– Verify that individual functions, classes, and components behave correctly before integrating them with the rest of the application.</span></li>
<li><a href="/glossary/integration-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>Integration tests</span></u></strong></a><span> – Ensure different services, modules, APIs, and databases work together correctly across your application.</span></li>
<li><a href="/glossary/end-to-end-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>End-to-end tests</span></u></strong></a><strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"> </span></strong><span>– Validate complete user workflows to confirm the application behaves as expected from the user's perspective.</span></li>
<li><a href="/glossary/regression-testing-in-software-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>Regression tests</span></u></strong></a><span> – Automatically detect issues introduced by new features, bug fixes, or refactoring before changes reach production.</span></li>
<li><a href="/glossary/performance-testing" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><strong><u><span>Performance tests</span></u></strong></a><strong><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;"> </span></strong><span>– Measure your application's speed, stability, and scalability under realistic workloads when performance is critical.</span></li>
</ul>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><strong><span>Worth knowing</span></strong><span>:</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Zencoder uses AI to automate testing across your entire application, helping you identify issues earlier while decreasing the effort required to create and maintain tests. Here's what it can do:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Create tests from natural language prompts</span></strong><span>, reducing the need to write test code manually</span></li>
<li><span>Understand your application and validate functionality across the </span><strong><span>UI, APIs, databases, and other system layers</span></strong></li>
<li><strong><span>Keep test suites up to date</span></strong><span> automatically as your codebase evolves</span></li>
<li><span>Cover everything from</span><strong><span> individual components to complete end-to-end user workflows</span></strong></li>
<li><strong><span>Identify high-risk code paths</span></strong><span> and uncover edge cases by simulating realistic user behavior</span></li>
</ul>
<h3>6. Improve Documentation and Knowledge Sharing</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Keeping documentation up to date makes it easier to find information, understand unfamiliar code, and onboard new developers. </span><a href="https://dam-cdn.atl.orangelogic.com/AssetLink/v26bjt7fvawounqfnlx4745445ng160f/fl_keep_metadata/CSD-7616_Document_ADO_State_of_DevEx_Survey-FINAL.pdf" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>Atlassian's 2024 State of Developer Experience report</span></u></a><span> found that inefficient documentation is a </span><strong><span>major productivity barrier for 41% of developers</span></strong><span>. Here’s how to improve documentation:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Keep architecture documentation up to date</span></strong><span> – Document your system architecture, key design decisions, and important dependencies so they're easy to understand.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Maintain your READMEs</span></strong><span> – Regularly update project READMEs with setup instructions, configuration details, and usage examples.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Automate API documentation</span></strong><span> – Generate API documentation directly from your code to keep it accurate as your application evolves.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Create onboarding guides </span></strong><span>– Document your development environment, workflows, and common tasks to help new developers get up to speed quickly.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Use AI to maintain documentation </span></strong><span>– Let AI generate documentation, summarize code changes, and keep existing documentation up to date as your codebase evolves.</span></li>
</ul>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><strong><span>Worth knowing</span></strong><span>: To find the best AI tools for automating code documentation, check out our article “</span><a href="/blog/best-code-documentation-tools" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>10 Best Code Documentation Tools to Simplify Your Workflow</span></u></a><span>”.</span></p>
<h3>7. Measure Productivity Beyond Lines of Code</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>AI can generate code more quickly than humans, making traditional productivity metrics like lines of code or commit counts less meaningful. </span><a href="https://www.gitclear.com/ai_assistant_code_quality_2025_research" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><u><span>GitClear's 2024 research</span></u></a><span> found that refactored code dropped from 25% of changed lines in 2021 to </span><strong><span>less than 10% in 2024</span></strong><span>, while copied code increased from </span><strong><span>8.3% to 12.3%</span></strong><span>.</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>This suggests that AI is helping developers write more code, but not necessarily better code. It’s more important to measure the value and complexity of your work than the amount of code you produce.</span></p>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Here’s how to measure your productivity more effectively:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Focus on the complexity of your work </span></strong><span>– Solving a difficult bug, designing a new feature, or refactoring a complex module often delivers far more value than producing a large amount of code.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Watch for unnecessary code churn</span></strong><span> – If you frequently rewrite, delete, or revert AI-generated code, it's a sign you should spend more time reviewing prompts, validating outputs, or refining your approach.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Track where AI saves you the most time</span></strong><span> – Notice which tasks AI consistently accelerates, such as writing tests, documentation, boilerplate code, or debugging, so you can make it a regular part of your workflow.</span></li>
</ul>
<h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Common Developer Workflow Mistakes to Avoid</span></h2>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Even the best tools and processes won't improve productivity if common workflow mistakes keep getting in the way. Here are some of the most common mistakes to keep in mind:</span></p>
<ul>
<li><strong><span>Treating AI as a replacement instead of an assistant</span></strong><span> – AI is great at speeding up development, but it shouldn't replace engineering judgment. Blindly accepting suggestions often leads to technical debt and hidden bugs.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Jumping straight into coding without a plan</span></strong><span> – Starting implementation before understanding the problem often results in unnecessary rewrites and scope creep. Spending a few minutes planning usually saves hours of rework.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Ignoring technical debt for too long</span></strong><span> – Continuously postponing refactoring, dependency updates, or infrastructure improvements makes future development slower and more expensive. Address technical debt regularly instead of waiting until it becomes a major problem.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Optimizing too early </span></strong><span>– Spending time perfecting code before validating that it solves the right problem can waste valuable development time. Focus on delivering working solutions first, then optimize where it matters.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Working in isolation for too long </span></strong><span>– Waiting days or weeks before sharing progress increases the risk of duplicate work, merge conflicts, and missed feedback. Frequent communication helps teams catch problems earlier.</span></li>
<li><strong><span>Reinventing existing solutions</span></strong><span> – Building custom tools or features that already exist can consume time without adding real value. Check your existing codebase, internal libraries, and trusted open-source solutions before starting from scratch.</span></li>
</ul>

<h2 style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>FAQ:</span></h2>
<h3>1. What should you automate first in a developer workflow?</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Start with repetitive, time-consuming tasks that provide consistent value, such as running tests, linting, formatting, dependency updates, and code reviews. Automating these tasks reduces manual effort, helps prevent errors, and gives developers more time to focus on building features.</span></p>
<h3>2. How often should development workflows be reviewed and updated?</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Review development workflows regularly, especially after introducing new tools, team processes, or major architectural changes. A quarterly review is often enough to identify bottlenecks, remove unnecessary steps, and ensure your workflow continues to support your team's goals.</span></p>
<h3>3. What is developer toil?</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Developer toil is repetitive, manual work that takes time away from higher-value engineering tasks, such as configuring environments, handling routine deployments, or performing maintenance tasks.</span></p>
<h3>4. What is the 80/20 rule in coding?</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>The 80/20 rule, or the Pareto principle, suggests that roughly 20% of your code or architectural decisions can cause 80% of the problems affecting productivity, quality, and scalability. Identifying and improving these high-impact areas can deliver bigger workflow improvements than trying to optimize everything at once.</span></p>
<h3>5. How can you identify bottlenecks in a developer workflow?</h3>
<p style="line-height: 1.2;"><span>Look at each stage of your development process and identify where work regularly gets delayed or piles up. For example, if pull requests consistently wait days for review, your code review process may be slowing down the entire workflow.</span></p>
